research_question: In women with recurrent urinary tract infections, do cranberry products (juice, capsules, tablets or powder, any dose) compared with placebo, no treatment or a non-active control reduce the proportion of participants experiencing at least one symptomatic, culture-verified UTI during follow-up?
treatment_label: Cranberry product (juice, capsules, tablets or powder, any dose)
control_label: Placebo, no treatment or non-active control
outcome_description: Number of participants with at least one symptomatic, culture-verified urinary tract infection during the whole study follow-up period (events) out of the number of participants analysed in each arm (total). Participants, not episodes; intention-to-treat sample where reported, otherwise the analysed sample as reported by the paper. Where UTI is reported at several follow-up times, the total over the whole study period (longest on-treatment follow-up) is used. Multi-arm trials with several cranberry arms are combined by summing events and participants; only placebo/no-treatment arms serve as control. Asymptomatic bacteriuria, bacteriuria alone, symptoms-only definitions, adverse effects, adherence, dropouts, urinary E. coli counts and antibiotic use are not pooled.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g (equivalently a risk ratio below 1) means fewer women experienced a symptomatic, culture-verified UTI in the cranberry arm than in the placebo/no-treatment arm — i.e. the result favours cranberry.
search_queries: cranberry recurrent urinary tract infection randomized controlled trial women
cranberry juice capsules prevention UTI placebo trial
proanthocyanidin cranberry supplement urinary tract infection prophylaxis trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in women with a history of recurrent urinary tract infection (e.g. 2 or more episodes in a year or 3 or more in two years), including both currently infected and infection-free women at baseline
Compares any cranberry product (juice, capsules, tablets, powder, any dose) with placebo, no treatment or another non-active control
Reports quantitative data allowing calculation of the number of participants with at least one symptomatic, culture-verified UTI out of the number analysed in each arm
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, narrative review, theoretical or protocol paper)

No comparison between a cranberry treatment arm and a placebo/no-treatment/non-active control arm (e.g. cranberry versus antibiotic or cranberry versus probiotic only), or not a randomised controlled trial

No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no participant-level event counts, proportions, or odds/risk ratios for symptomatic culture-verified UTI; episode counts or incidence rates only)
Population outside scope (children, pregnant women, institutionalised older people, neurogenic bladder, indwelling catheters) or completely unrelated to cranberry and urinary tract infection
moderators_to_extract: Baseline infection status (currently infected vs infection-free)
Sample size category and risk-of-bias rating
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio with a random-effects model (DerSimonian–Laird or REML) on participant-level event counts; RR < 1 favours cranberry. Combine multiple cranberry arms by summing events and totals; use only placebo/no-treatment arms as control.
